article_sentences: Several areas in Bhadradri Kothagudem and Khammam districts witnessed intermittent drizzle on Wednesday under the influence of Cyclone Arnab.
A control room was set up at the Bhadrachalam sub-Collector’s office to respond to emergencies, which can be reached at 08743-232444.
Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in Bhadradri Kothagudem district remained closed as a precautionary measure.

He also visited vulnerable areas in the temple town to assess the situation.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab weakens, but heavy rain and hailstorms threaten several states
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab weakens, but heavy rain and hailstorms threaten several states
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Delhi-NCR and several other parts of India are bracing for unsettled weather on Thursday, October 29, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting hailstorms, thunderstorms and heavy to very heavy rainfall in multiple states as Cyclone Arnab weakens after landfall.
New Delhi: The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in six states on Thursday, October 29, even as Cyclone Arnab weakens after making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts.
Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab are also under a weather alert, with thunderstorms and isolated hailstorms possible.
Gusty winds and lightning are expected in several parts of the country.
According to the IMD bulletin issued on Wednesday, isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely in Bihar, Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, east Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha on October 29.
Heavy rainfall is also forecast at isolated places in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, coastal Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal and Sikkim.
Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab could experience thunderstorms accompanied by hailstorms at isolated locations.
The IMD has also forecast thundersqualls, with wind speeds of 50–60 kmph, in these regions and Jharkhand.

East Rajasthan could see isolated hailstorms, while parts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, coastal Andhra Pradesh and other regions may experience lightning, thunderstorms and gusty winds.
Rainfall is expected to remain fairly widespread to widespread over east Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi on October 29 and 30.
Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam during the early hours of Wednesday.
The IMD said the landfall process was completed by 8.30 am on October 28, with the system moving entirely over land.

stories.headline: Ashok accuses State Election Commission of printing 90 lakh voter cards after announcement of SIR; SEC denies charge
stories.title: Ashok accuses State Election Commission of printing 90 lakh voter cards after announcement of SIR; SEC denies charge
stories.summary: Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok has accused the State Election Commission of violating norms to facilitate irregularities in the proposed GBA polls by printing 90 lakh voters’ identity cards in Bengaluru at a cost of ₹20 crore after the announcement of Special Intensive Revision by the Election Commission of India
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok has accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of violating norms to facilitate irregularities in the proposed GBA polls by printing 90 lakh voters’ identity cards in Bengaluru at a cost of ₹20 crore after the announcement of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India.
Alleging that the Congress government was involved in these irregularities, Mr. Ashok demanded a CBI probe into the episode.
However, the SEC strongly denied these allegations by stating that the tenders had been floated before the announcement of SIR and that it had acted within its legal mandate.
Addressing a press conference in Bengaluru, Mr. Ashok alleged that the SEC had printed 90 lakh cards, though the total number of voters in Bengaluru had been pegged at around 59 lakh after the SIR.
Pointing out that the SEC was now left with an additional 31 lakh voters identity cards, he described these additional cards as “bogus” and alleged that they would be used for “vote theft”.
He alleged that the Congress government had got this done to commit irregularities in the proposed election to GBA.

“The State Election Commission did this though it had filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court stating that elections to local bodies would be held only after the SIR and after the new voters’ list is prepared,“ he said.
Denying the allegations, SEC Secretary Amaresh H. said the tender was called before the SIR was announced.
Mr. Amaresh said the tender was issued under Rule 26 of the Greater Bengaluru Governance (Registration of Electors) Rules, 2025, which provides for the printing of voter identity cards.
He said the SEC had acted within its legal mandate and that the SIR did not require it to suspend its work relating to local body electoral processes.
“The SIR is not binding on the State Election Commission in the manner being suggested.
Local body elections and elections conducted by the Election Commission of India are governed by different frameworks,” he said.

stories.headline: Allahabad HC in chaos over seat argument, lawyers' body writes to Chief Justice
stories.title: Allahabad HC in chaos over seat argument, lawyers' body writes to Chief Justice
stories.summary: Allahabad HC in chaos over seat argument, lawyers' body writes to Chief Justice
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: The Allahabad High Court Bar Association has approached the Chief Justice over a lawyer's alleged humiliation in court.
The dispute has triggered boycott discussions amid concerns about advocates' dignity.

The Allahabad High Court Bar Association has threatened to boycott the court of Justice Ajay Bhanot over the alleged humiliation of a lawyer during proceedings in Court No. 49, accusing the judge of undermining the dignity of the legal fraternity.

In a letter dated October 27 to the Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court, the association demanded appropriate action and warned that it would boycott the judge’s court if the matter was not addressed.

The letter, signed by Bar Association president Dr CP Upadhyay and general secretary Santosh Kumar Mishra, detailed an incident involving a district Superintendent of Police (SP), an Additional Government Advocate (AGA) and a lawyer.
According to the letter, Justice Bhanot had directed that a separate chair be placed in the row behind the lawyers for police officers or other senior officials appearing in his courtroom.
During proceedings on Tuesday, an SP-rank officer was seated behind the AGA when a lawyer politely asked him to move to the designated seat, saying it was not his place.
The AGA allegedly rebuked the lawyer and threatened to complain to the judge when he arrived.
After Justice Bhanot entered the courtroom, the AGA raised the issue with him.
The association alleged that the judge pointed a finger at the lawyer, used harsh language and ordered that he be sent to jail.
When the lawyer asked the police officer to forgive him, the judge allegedly insisted that he apologise to the SP.
The lawyer subsequently apologised to the officer, the letter claimed.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Cancels Bail Of Man Accused Of Sharing Sensitive Military Information With Pakistan
stories.title: Supreme Court Cancels Bail Of Man Accused Of Sharing Sensitive Military Information With Pakistan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday set aside a Rajasthan High Court order that had granted regular bail to an accused in an espionage case solely because the grounds of arrest were not furnished to him in writing.

“A hyper-technical objection regarding the form or mode of communicating grounds of arrest cannot be treated as a self-executing, blanket key to unlock regular bail, bypassing the core parameters governing bail jurisprudence,” the bench held.

A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B Varale made the observations while directing the respondent Jhabra Ram to surrender within two weeks from the date of the order, while reiterating that communication of grounds of arrest is a crucial constitutional and statutory safeguard, but held that the record showed substantial and effective compliance in the case, and that no prejudice had been found.

The case deals with offences under Sections 3 and 9 of the Official Secrets Act, 1923 (OSA), and Sections 152 and 238(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), alleging that the respondent was in contact with foreign handlers belonging to a Pakistani intelligence agency and was transmitting sensitive military photographs, videos and troop movement details from Pokhran and Jaisalmer in exchange for financial benefits.
The respondent was served several notices calling him to appear before interrogation centres, before the FIR was registered.
Subsequently, an FIR was registered against him which led to his arrest on 30 January 2026.
The Arrest Memo was read over to him in the presence of two witnesses and bears his signature.
At the same time, his brother was also informed telephonically of his arrest, as recorded in an Arrest Information Memo.

On 31 January 2026, the respondent was produced before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate where he opposed police custody remand on merits, but neither he nor his counsel raised any grievance about non-communication of grounds of arrest.

His regular bail plea was rejected by the Additional District and Sessions Judge on 10 March 2026, which held that the signed Arrest Memo amounted to compliance in substance with Section 47 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS).
Later, on 18 May 2026, the High Court granted bail on the basis that the grounds of arrest were not furnished in writing before or at the time of remand.
It held that oral intimation or case diary entries did not satisfy Section 47 BNSS in light of Mihir Rajesh Shah v State of Maharashtra.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays Punjab & Haryana HC Order Restraining Rohtak Courts From Hearing Bail Pleas In DHL Real Estate Scam Case
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Punjab & Haryana HC Order Restraining Rohtak Courts From Hearing Bail Pleas In DHL Real Estate Scam Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has stayed a Punjab and Haryana High Court order restraining judicial officers in Rohtak Sessions Division from entertaining bail applications in a case involving an alleged large-scale real estate investment scam in which investors were allegedly cheated of crores of rupees.
A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran passed the order on October 27 while hearing a special leave petition filed challenging the High Court's September 30 order.
The Court issued notice, returnable in four weeks, and stayed the operation of the impugned order in the meantime.
“Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.
Dasti service, in addition, is permitted.
In the meantime, there shall be stay of operation of the impugned order dated 30.09.2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in CRM M-42815/2026”, the Court ordered.

The High Court had passed the order while hearing an anticipatory bail petition filed by Subhash Gupta, a partner of Gupta Property Developers, Shivji, in connection with an FIR under Sections 420, 120-B and 506 of the IPC, corresponding to Sections 318(4), 61 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

In its order, the High Court had expressed serious concern over the investigation, observing that attempts had been made to shield the main accused, who are accused of cheating numerous investors of crores of rupees by collecting money for real estate projects without delivering possession or returning the invested amounts.
The High Court had noted that, despite earlier directions, the investigation had not proceeded properly.

It noted that a Special Investigation Team headed by Rohtak Superintendent of Police Gaurav Rajpurohit was investigating the case and that Kuldeep Kumar Tahlan, a director of DHL Infratech Private Limited, and Gurvinder Jeet Singh, an employee of Gupta Property Developers, had been arrested.
The Court noted that Kuldeep Kumar Tahlan had been granted bail, whereas Gurvinder Jeet Singh's bail plea had been dismissed by the courts at Rohtak.

It further observed that three directors of DHL Infratech and its authorised signatory, Sidhant, had been granted interim anticipatory bail by the same presiding officer who had dismissed the bail plea of the petitioner before the High Court.

Dasti service, in addition, is permitted.

stories.headline: Union Cabinet approves ₹7,396 crore until FY31 for PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana
stories.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹7,396 crore until FY31 for PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana
stories.summary: As part of capacity building under the scheme, the Centre will train elected representatives, officials in the 3-tier panchayati raj system
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, a new scheme to enable panchayats identify their local resources and constraints, and prepare development plans based on their specific needs.
As part of capacity building under the scheme, the Centre will also train elected representatives as well as officials in the 3-tier panchayati raj system.

Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw called it a paradigm shift from prescription-based schemes to a model focused on local-level capacity building and planning.
The scheme is approved for implementation from current fiscal till 2030-31, with an outlay of ₹7,395.55 crore — Central share of ₹4,869.48 crore and State share of ₹2,526.07 crore.

A major focus of the scheme is capacity-building of elected representatives as general and specialised training will be provided to elected representatives to improve their functioning and governance capabilities, he said.
The scheme seeks to financially empower panchayats through better utilisation of Finance Commission grants and mobilisation of own-source revenue, to make them more self-reliant, he added.

Sources said that though it is a new scheme, but it has also all the features of the previous Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), including its many components like the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), which was not extended after it ended in FY26.
Under RGSA, the Centre had released to States ₹800.17 crore in 2023-24, ₹670.40 crore in 2024-25 and ₹730.75 crore in April-February of 2025-26.

The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana will be implemented through the respective State governments in which States and Union Territories will submit Annual Action Plans specifying activities, priorities and requirements in accordance with the scheme’s objectives and guidelines, an official statement said.
The designated Central Empowered Committee will appraise and approve these plans in accordance with applicable procedures and norms.
The Central Government and States will undertake activities within their respective areas of responsibility, supported by coordination, technical assistance, monitoring and review.
Existing institutional, capacity-building, digital, and communication systems will support implementation at the grassroots level, it said.
